:::{#thm-reed-solomon-list-size}
#### A bound on the list size of a Reed--Solomon code

Let $C$ be the [Reed--Solomon code](error-correcting-codes.qmd#def-reed-solomon-code) with length $n$ and $k$ message symbols,
and let $e \in \{0, 1, \ldots, n - k\}$.
Then every received word has at most

$$\frac{\binom{n}{k}}{\binom{n - e}{k}}$$

codewords within [Hamming distance](error-correcting-codes.qmd#def-hamming-distance) $e$.
So $C$ is $(e, L)$-list-decodable for every $L$ at least the value above.

:::

::: proof

Fix a received word $r$ and let $S$ be the codewords $c$ with $\hamdist{c}{r} \le e$.
Count the pairs $(c, T)$,
where $c \in S$ and $T$ is a choice of $k$ positions at which $c$ and $r$ agree.

Each $c \in S$ differs from $r$ in at most $e$ positions,
so it agrees with $r$ in at least $n - e$ positions.
Since $n - e \ge k$,
it has at least $\binom{n - e}{k}$ choices of $T$.
So there are at least $|S| \binom{n - e}{k}$ pairs.

Now fix a choice $T$ of $k$ positions.
Two distinct codewords that both agree with $r$ on $T$ agree with each other on $T$.
By [the distance theorem](error-correcting-codes.qmd#thm-reed-solomon-distance), distinct codewords differ in at least $n - k + 1$ positions,
so they agree in at most $k - 1$ positions,
which is fewer than $k$.
So at most one codeword $c$ agrees with $r$ on $T$.
There are $\binom{n}{k}$ choices of $T$,
so there are at most $\binom{n}{k}$ pairs.

Combine the two counts:

$$|S| \binom{n - e}{k} \le \binom{n}{k}.$$

Divide both sides by $\binom{n - e}{k}$, which is nonzero because $n - e \ge k$.

:::
